subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw allow Docker sandbox containers to start without `no-new-privileges` on hosts where that hardening flag prevents even `/usr/bin/sleep` from execing?
rationale: The report is actionable, but the fix is a security-boundary product choice: a silent fallback improves availability but weakens hardening, while fail-closed preserves security but leaves affected sandboxes unusable.

options.title: Explicit opt-out with warnings
options.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` as the default, add a dangerous config opt-out, and report the weaker posture through doctor/security diagnostics.

options.title: Fail closed with better diagnostics
options.body: Keep the hardening mandatory and improve status/session errors so affected operators can identify the Docker host incompatibility without patching dist output.

options.title: Automatic retry fallback
options.body: Retry container startup without the flag only for the detected EPERM failure, accepting more availability risk and requiring careful audit visibility.

recommendation.title: Explicit opt-out with warnings
recommendation.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` as the default, add a dangerous config opt-out, and report the weaker posture through doctor/security diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current Docker sandbox create-args path and have recent adjacent sandbox maintenance history.
